accepted.s: What is identified as the biggest drawback of the multiple-rate structure under GST?
o: Delay in settlement of IGST between the Union and the States
Dependence of States on Finance Commission devolution
Misclassification of goods and services and classification disputes
Complete exclusion of petroleum products from taxation
accepted.x: The multiple-rate structure creates difficulties in classifying goods and services, resulting in frequent classification disputes.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the specific weakness associated with a tax structure.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: The four-slab structure of GST was originally intended to be:
o: A permanent arrangement for all goods and services
A mechanism for distributing IGST among States
A structure applicable only to petroleum products
accepted.x: The four-slab GST structure was conceived as a transitional arrangement rather than a permanent structure.
accepted.tq: Test the intended character of a policy arrangement rather than its numerical details.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Under the GST 2.0 rate structure introduced on 22 September 2025, the principal slabs were reduced to:
accepted.x: GST 2.0, introduced on 22 September 2025, reduced the structure to 5%, 18% and 40% slabs.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact date and numerical slab combination.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Which of the following continue to remain outside the GST framework?
accepted.x: Petroleum and electricity remain outside the GST framework.
accepted.tq: Use confusable sector exclusions to distinguish items inside and outside a tax regime.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT):
1. It was created through the Finance Act, 2024.
2. Its Principal Bench is located in New Delhi.
3. Its membership includes a President and Technical Members from the Centre and the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. GSTAT was created through the Finance Act, 2024, has its Principal Bench at New Delhi, and includes a President and Centre- and State-level Technical Members.
accepted.tq: Combine legislative, locational and institutional-composition facts in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: The first President of the GST Appellate Tribunal was a former Chief Justice of the:
accepted.x: The first President of GSTAT was a former Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court.
accepted.tq: Apply the person-and-office trap by matching the office-holder with the correct institution.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the operational timeline of GSTAT?
o: Formally launched in September 2025 and hearings commenced in December 2025
Formally launched in December 2025 and hearings commenced in September 2026
Formally launched in April 2024 and hearings commenced in September 2025
Formally launched in September 2026 and hearings commenced in December 2026
accepted.x: GSTAT was formally launched in September 2025, while hearings began in December 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-second event sequence to eliminate reversed timelines.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Appeals before the GST Appellate Tribunal are to be filed online within:
accepted.x: Appeals before GSTAT are to be filed online within three months.
accepted.tq: Recall the prescribed time limit using close numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: What was an important consequence of the earlier absence of GSTAT benches?
o: Appeals accumulated in the High Courts
Petroleum products were brought under GST
GST collections were transferred entirely to the States
The four GST slabs were abolished immediately
accepted.x: Before GSTAT benches became available, GST-related appeals accumulated in the High Courts.
accepted.tq: Link an institutional gap with its direct administrative consequence.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: An inverted duty structure arises when:
o: Input tax is higher than output tax, resulting in blocked credit
Input and output taxes are equal but refunds are prohibited
Output tax is higher than input tax and exports are taxed fully
Output tax is collected by the State instead of the Centre
accepted.x: An inverted duty structure exists when the tax paid on inputs exceeds the tax charged on output, leading to blocked credit; refunds are allowed in such cases.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to the relationship between input tax and output tax.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Domestic GST refunds surged by what percentage in August 2026 due to inverted duties?
accepted.x: Domestic refunds increased by 72.6% in August 2026, largely because of inverted-duty claims.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive percentage with ascending numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: Which practice is characteristic of the ITC fraud involving bogus entities?
o: Paying output tax twice on genuine transactions
Issuing invoices without actual supply of goods or services
Using only government invoices for exports
Claiming refunds on petroleum products outside GST
accepted.x: Bogus entities issue invoices without any corresponding supply in order to fraudulently claim input tax credit.
accepted.tq: Identify the fraudulent mechanism from a practical transaction scenario.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s: The fake-registration and scrap-bill network involved in ITC fraud operated across which group of States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
accepted.x: The reported network used fake registrations and scrap bills across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related geographical combinations.
accepted.sec: Unresolved issues - rates, petroleum, GSTAT, inverted duty, ITC fraud

accepted.s:

Exclusion of all State taxes from GST

accepted.s: In which month did monthly gross GST collections first exceed ₹2 lakh crore?
accepted.x: Monthly gross GST collections crossed ₹2 lakh crore for the first time in April 2024.
accepted.tq: Test a milestone date using close year alternatives.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s gross GST collection during FY 2024-25?
o: ₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹24.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.43 lakh crore per month
₹17.4 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.82 lakh crore per month
accepted.x: Gross GST collection in FY 2024-25 was ₹22.08 lakh crore, averaging ₹2.04 lakh crore per month.

accepted.s: Gross GST collection during April–December 2025 was:
accepted.x: Gross GST collection during April–December 2025 amounted to ₹17.4 lakh crore, showing 6.7% growth.
accepted.tq: Match the period, total and growth rate in a quantitative data question.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about GST collections in April 2026:
1. Gross GST collection reached a record ₹2.43 lakh crore.
2. Gross collection grew by 8.7%.
3. Net GST collection was ₹2.11 lakh crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct for April 2026: gross collection was ₹2.43 lakh crore, growth was 8.7%, and net collection was ₹2.11 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Test whether a complete set of related quantitative statements is internally consistent.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes GST collections during April–July 2026?
o: Gross ₹8.43 lakh crore, growth 10.1%, and net ₹7.21 lakh crore with growth 9.2%
Gross ₹17.4 lakh crore, growth 6.7%, and net ₹8.43 lakh crore with growth 10.1%
Gross ₹7.21 lakh crore, growth 9.2%, and net ₹8.43 lakh crore with growth 10.1%
Gross ₹8.43 lakh crore, growth 8.7%, and net ₹7.21 lakh crore with growth 14.8%
accepted.x: During April–July 2026, gross GST collection was ₹8.43 lakh crore, up 10.1%; net collection was ₹7.21 lakh crore, up 9.2%.
accepted.tq: Compare gross and net figures while preserving their correct order and growth rates.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST collections in August 2026:
1. Gross GST collection grew by 14.8%.
2. Net GST collection grew by 8.3%.
3. Domestic GST grew by 9.3%.
4. Import-side GST grew faster than domestic GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. August 2026 gross growth was 14.8%, net growth was 8.3%, domestic growth was 9.3%, and import-side GST grew faster than domestic GST.
accepted.tq: Combine headline growth, net growth and component-wise trends in a coded question.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: The gross GST collection in April–December 2025 was what proportion of the FY 2024-25 annual gross collection, approximately?
o: More than the full annual collection
accepted.x: ₹17.4 lakh crore is approximately 79% of ₹22.08 lakh crore, which is about three-fourths and clearly more than one-half but less than the full annual amount.
accepted.tq: Use approximate ratio comparison rather than merely recalling an isolated figure.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: Which statement best explains the reported weakness in GST buoyancy despite the August 2026 rate revision?
o: All States had recorded growth below the national average
Domestic GST had grown faster than import-side GST
Imports had stopped contributing to GST revenue
Revenue loss from the rate cut was still awaiting gains from higher volume
accepted.x: GST buoyancy remained weak because the revenue loss from the rate cut had not yet been fully offset by volume gains.
accepted.tq: Connect a policy rate change with its short-term revenue effect and delayed volume response.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s December 2025 net GST growth exceeded the national growth by approximately:

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model?
1. It uses a risk matrix.
2. Its Legal-AI assistant was trained on approximately 22,000 judgments.
3. It has dealt with more than 13,700 cases.
4. It is being studied by several other States.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The model uses a risk matrix, a Legal-AI assistant trained on about 22,000 judgments, and has covered more than 13,700 cases; other States are studying it.
accepted.tq: Test a technology initiative through its components, scale and adoption by other States.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: Which group of States is specifically mentioned as studying Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model?
o: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Kerala and Assam
Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Haryana, Assam and Madhya Pradesh
Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Kerala and Goa
Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha, Punjab and Gujarat
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Kerala, Assam and other States are studying Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model.
accepted.tq: Recall a multi-State institutional-adoption list without substituting neighbouring States.
accepted.sec: GST collections trend - national and AP

accepted.s: One major fiscal consequence for States of surrendering independent indirect-tax powers under GST has been:
o: Greater dependence on transfers because of weak own revenues
Automatic equalisation of revenues among all States
Complete elimination of State taxation powers
accepted.x: The surrender of independent indirect-tax powers, combined with weak own revenues, has increased States’ dependence on transfers.
accepted.tq: Link the loss of fiscal autonomy with the resulting dependence on transfers.
accepted.sec: Impact on States - autonomy, compensation dependency, consuming vs producing

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical concentration of GST buoyancy:
1. Only 16 States and Union Territories recorded post-settlement GST growth above the national average.
2. Manufacturing States tend to gain from this pattern.
3. States with a large unorganised sector depend on Finance Commission devolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. GST buoyancy was above the national average in only 16 States/UTs; manufacturing States gained, while unorganised-sector States relied more on Finance Commission devolution.
accepted.tq: Combine a numerical count with distributional consequences across State types.
accepted.sec: Impact on States - autonomy, compensation dependency, consuming vs producing

accepted.s: The destination principle of GST generally favours:
o: States with the highest rates of State excise duty
Producing States because tax is collected at the point of manufacture
Consuming States because taxation follows the place of consumption
accepted.x: GST follows the destination principle, under which consuming States benefit because revenue is associated with the place of consumption.
accepted.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.
accepted.sec: Impact on States - autonomy, compensation dependency, consuming vs producing

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh, being a consuming State, benefits from GST primarily through:
o: State excise on petroleum under GST
Abolition of its own tax revenue
accepted.x: As a consuming State, Andhra Pradesh benefits from the destination principle through IGST settlement.
accepted.tq: Apply the destination principle to the fiscal position of a particular State.
accepted.sec: Impact on States - autonomy, compensation dependency, consuming vs producing

accepted.s: Which statement about Andhra Pradesh’s net GST collection in December 2025 is correct?
o: It was ₹2,652 crore, grew by 5.78%, was the highest December collection, and marked the ninth consecutive month above the previous year.
It was ₹2,652 crore, grew by 5.61%, and was the first month above the previous year.
It was ₹13,282 crore, grew by 21%, and marked the ninth consecutive month above the previous year.
It was ₹16,452.62 crore, grew by 18.05%, and was the highest-ever monthly collection.
accepted.x: December 2025 net GST was ₹2,652 crore, up 5.78%; it was Andhra Pradesh’s highest December collection and the ninth consecutive month above the corresponding previous-year level, despite GST 2.0 rate cuts.
accepted.tq: Use a long precise option and verify its figure, growth rate and sequential record together.
